name: Mofazzal Haider Chaudhury
contribution: Mofazzal Haider Chaudhury was a Bengali linguist, essayist, educator, and scholar of Bangla literature. He joined the University of Dhaka in 1955, wrote works including Rabi Parikrama, and received the Bangla Academy Prize in 1971.
context: Born in 1926 in Khalishpur in Noakhali, Chaudhury studied Bangla at Calcutta University and Dhaka University before teaching and researching at the University of Dhaka. His work connected language study, literary criticism, and public intellectual life in East Pakistan.
impact: Chaudhury is remembered both for his contribution to Bangla language and literature and as one of the intellectuals abducted and killed on 14 December 1971. His career and death connect cultural scholarship with the violence and memory of the Liberation War.

faq.question: How is Mofazzal Haider Chaudhury connected to 1971?
faq.answer: He was abducted and killed on 14 December 1971, in the final days of the Liberation War, and is remembered as a martyred intellectual.
